thread.title_full: Politico Caves After Trump White House Gives Outlet 48 Hours to Correct Report

author: Jimmy Parker
title: Politico Caves After Trump White House Gives Outlet 48 Hours to Correct Report
text:
Politico Walks Back the Claim
Politico issued a correction after the White House gave the outlet a 48-hour ultimatum. The dispute centered on a report about Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and an interview between Fox News host Sean Hannity and then-Press Secretary Katie Zacharia. Earlier reporting claimed Wiles was responsible for coordinating that interview. The updated item said the story and its headline had mischaracterized her role. It added that follow-up reporting indicated Wiles did not play a direct role in setting up the interview. That is a meaningful correction, especially because the Hannity appearance was widely viewed as the last nail in the coffin for Zacharia’s historically short run behind the press podium. The media world has many ways to describe a retreat, but “correction” is the word Politico chose.
The White House Gave Politico 48 Hours
On Monday, Trump’s counsel, William Scharf, sent a letter to Politico’s Global Editor-in-Chief Jonathan Greenberger. Scharf said Politico published a series of articles between October 14 and 17 that were “demonstrably false and defamatory” and designed to manufacture a story of dysfunction and infighting inside the White House. He said senior officials and the President had issued direct, on-the-record refutations, and that documentary evidence had also been provided. Yet, in his telling, Politico published the claims anyway and then hid behind anonymous sources. Scharf demanded prompt corrections or retractions, a public apology to Trump and Wiles, and removal of the false reports from Politico’s digital archives. He gave the outlet 48 hours to respond. If it failed, he said the administration would review its relationship with Politico and consider other legal remedies. His message was blunt: “Freedom of the press is not a professional exemption from accountability.”
A Tense Relationship Gets Tighter
The dispute comes after a rough stretch between the Trump administration and Politico. Earlier this year, Politico was banned from the White House along with CNN and MS NOW. A federal judge later granted the outlets temporary relief while the case moves through the courts. That means this correction arrived in an already tense relationship, where even a newsroom update can come with a legal timer attached. Scharf’s letter went beyond asking for a quiet edit. It demanded a prominent public apology to the President and Wiles, along with the removal of the reporting from Politico’s digital archives. In Washington, apparently, correcting the record can involve considerably more paperwork than simply pressing the update button.
Trump’s Other Media Settlements
The article also points to several other legal victories involving major media and technology companies. Last year, Trump reached a $16 million settlement with CBS parent company Paramount after the outlet’s deceptive editing of a Kamala Harris interview on 60 Minutes during the 2024 election cycle. In 2024, he received a $15 million payout from ABC News after suing the network and host George Stephanopoulos over repeated statements that Trump had been found “liable for rape.” In January 2025, Trump reached a settlement with Meta for roughly $25 million after the suspension of his social media accounts. The report says most of the money from these cases will fund Trump’s future presidential library.
